# State, 2026-11-04 (session 3, end)

## Where things stand

`main` at `d6a6f5a`. Three PRs are open, each cut from `main`. The full gate passed on each branch
before it was committed. Checkout is on `github-governance-eval-suites`, tree clean.

| PR | Branch | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| #69 | `terraform-validate-claim` | Anchored `validate-actually-run`; stale `terraform validate` claim replaced in `evals/README.md` and `evals/terraform-secure-iac/README.md` |
| #70 | `evidence-synthesizer-embedded-instruction` | es-04 option A: template Procedure sentence, `flags-embedded-instruction` source, suite README |
| #71 | `github-governance-eval-suites` | `evals/gh_stub.py`, token stripping and stub install in `run_eval.py`, `check_evals.py` unmeasured relaxation, grs-01..04 and gog-01..04 suites, doc updates, 64 citations renumbered |

`evals/README.md` was split between #69 (tsi paragraph) and #71 (no-suite paragraph). They touch
different lines, so merge order does not matter.

A backup of the pre-split working tree is in the session scratchpad (`bak/work.tar`). It will not
survive; the PRs hold everything.

## Token question, settled

The leaked `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not in the working tree, any local-ref commit, or `origin/main`. Across
2,439 committed `run.jsonl` transcripts, no executed GitHub write. Two write attempts, both HTTP 404:
a POST to placeholder `OWNER/REPO` and a `gh api search/repositories -f` call. 25 `gh auth token`
calls read the token; where the value went was not checked beyond that. Rotate it if certainty is
wanted.

## Next

1. Merge #69, #70, #71 (user does the merges). Check CI and review threads first.
2. Paid runs, from a clone of the merged `main`:
   - First task and trigger runs of both GitHub suites.
   - Evidence-synthesizer rerun for es-04.
   - Optionally tsi.
   - Inspect `gh-calls.jsonl` of failing runs before attributing failures to the skill.
3. Item 4: a terraform-testing task suite (4 to 7 fixtures). Mechanical enough for Sonnet.

## How to run an eval here

- Run from a clone outside the home directory, so `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is not an ancestor.
- Commit first, and set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`.
- Task suite: `python3 evals/run_eval.py tasks --skill <name> --model sonnet --runs 3 --parallel 5
  --stamp <stamp> --graders-reviewed`. Then copy `results/raw/<stamp>` back and run `report`,
  `scrub`, and `snapshot --stamp <stamp>`.
- Trigger suite: `triggers --skill <name> --model sonnet --runs 3 --parallel 5 --stamp <stamp>`.
- Delete the `home/` and `workspace/` sandboxes afterwards.

## Verification

`python3 scripts/check_skills.py && python3 scripts/check_evals.py &&
python3 scripts/check_citations.py && python3 scripts/check_content_only.py &&
uv run --frozen ruff check . && uv run --frozen ruff format --check . && uv run --frozen ty check .`
plus `npx markdownlint-cli2@0.23.2` over changed `*.md` files. Check each script's exit code.

## Open questions

- Is an unrun skill task suite counted as unmeasured rather than failed? Changed in #71
  (`check_evals.py`); the user has not confirmed it. The PR body asks.
- Unconfirmed: grs-04 (make public) and gog-03 (add bypass actor) grade a decline as a pass, because
  both skills treat those changes as proposals. Both READMEs and the PR body say so.
- The grader simulator lived in the session scratchpad and is gone. To repeat the grader replay,
  recreate it: for each task, the stub plus scripted good and naive runs, graded with
  `run_eval.grade_assertion`.

        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history rather than the default single commit. The staleness half of this
          # check compares the commit a stamp recorded against the commits that have since
          # touched the skill it measured, and scripts/check_evals.py degrades a failed git
          # lookup to an empty string, which reads as "nothing changed". A shallow checkout
          # would therefore report every suite as fresh without having compared anything.
          fetch-depth: 0
      # No uv setup: the script is standard library only, and it needs git and bash, which
      # the runner image already provides. Not unconditionally --strict, because staleness
      # is a statement about when a measurement was last taken and a pull request that does
      # not touch a skill cannot fix it; a structural error in a suite is the part that has
      # to block regardless. A change to an eval's own tasks.json or assertions.json is the
      # case where the contributor causing the staleness can also resolve it before merge, so
      # the findings on exactly those suites fail as well, and the findings on every other
      # suite stay reported. The structural checks are also the slot a grader-command check
      # belongs in, which docs/controls.md records as still open.
      - name: Check eval suites
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          args=()
          while IFS= read -r suite; do
            args+=(--strict-suite "${suite}")
          done < <(git diff --name-only "${BASE_SHA:-origin/main}...HEAD" \
              | sed -nE 's#^evals/([^/]+)/(tasks|assertions)\.json$#\1#p' | sort -u)
          python3 scripts/check_evals.py "${args[@]}"

**Neither failure is a bug. Both are the workflow doing what it was designed to do, and neither can be fixed without a paid eval run.**

| PR | CI | Review threads |
|---|---|---|
| #69 | `Eval suites` fails. The other checks pass. | One unresolved CodeRabbit thread, "Major", on `assertions.json:30`. |
| #70 | All checks pass. CodeRabbit is skipping. | None. |
| #71 | `Eval suites` fails. The other checks pass. CodeRabbit is skipping. | None. |

**#69: stale stamp.** I haven't opened `check_evals.py`'s staleness logic, so this comes from the CI log and the workflow comment. Changing `assertions.json` makes the `evals/terraform-secure-iac` `2026-11-01` stamp stale, and `lint.yml` runs `--strict-suite` on any suite whose `tasks.json` or `assertions.json` changed. The log says the stamp predates `bcecbfb9a54d`. The CodeRabbit thread says the same thing and is valid. Clearing it needs a paid terraform-secure-iac task and trigger rerun, which you do from a clone outside your home directory. The assertion change makes the old stamp inapplicable, so there is no honest shortcut. Your alternatives are to merge with the red check, which `main` protection may or may not allow, or to hold #69 until the rerun. I haven't checked whether the ruleset requires this job.

**#71: new suites never run.** The log shows 0 suites failed and 0 staleness findings. It fails because grs and gog are new suites whose `assertions.json` or `tasks.json` is in the diff. They are reported as "never run, so nothing has measured this skill", and `--strict-suite` turns that into a failure. This is a consequence of the `check_evals.py` change in #71, which is the open question in your state file. The deadlock is that CI can't pass until the suites have run, and they can't run from a clone of merged `main` until #71 merges.

I disagree with letting that stand as is. The risk is that every future PR adding a skill suite hits this wall, so merging is only possible by overriding the check.

Two options:
1. **Exempt never-run suites from `--strict-suite`.** They would still show as unmeasured, but wouldn't block the PR that introduces them. This is a small change in `check_evals.py`, and it fits the workflow comment's reasoning: only block when the contributor can resolve it before merge.
2. **Keep it strict and override on #71.** This is simpler but sets a precedent.

I recommend option 1. It means editing #71, so tell me if you want it. Whether the ruleset requires the `Eval suites` job decides if either PR is mergeable at all. Check with `gh api repos/konstruktoid/agent-instructions-skills/rulesets`.

**#70** is green with no threads and can merge now.

Option 1 is implemented in `scripts/check_evals.py`; nothing is staged or committed.

- **The change:** `--strict-suite` now skips findings of the form "never run, so nothing has measured …". They still print as `unmeasured:` and still fail a full `--strict` run. Staleness findings on a changed suite still block, which is what #69 needs. A comment at the filter explains the deadlock, and the usage docstring at line 73 notes the exception.
- **Scope:** the exemption covers every never-run finding, not just skill suites. That includes agent templates, trigger-only routing and instructions documents. I think that's right, since the same deadlock applies to each, but it is wider than the #71 suites.
- **Verified:** `--strict-suite github-repository-security` and `--strict-suite github-organization-governance` both exit 0. Before the change, CI exited 1 on them. I did not run the full CI job against the GitHub-side diff.
- **Gate:** `check_skills`, `check_evals`, `check_citations`, `check_content_only`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `ty` all exit 0. I did not run markdownlint, because I changed no `*.md` files.
- **Test coverage:** `check_evals.py` has no tests that I looked for. I did not check whether the repo has any under a test directory.

The change is uncommitted on `github-governance-eval-suites`. To get #71's CI green, it needs a commit and a push, which you have to ask for. #69 stays red until the paid terraform-secure-iac rerun.
signed commit with a minimal commit messag
